investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T17:45–17:52Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the VM provisioning step.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any new remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free capacity. The failure is localized to the Kubernetes peer-pod VM resource layer in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' scheduler message across all three sibling checks over a ~7-minute window.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. If the affinity were broadened or more nodes were labeled, capacity could be restored without changing VM slot limits.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM quota or cloud-provider limit reached at the infrastructure layer beneath Kubernetes: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is typically backed by a cloud VM quota; if that quota is exhausted, the device plugin would report 0 allocatable units on the eligible nodes, producing the same scheduler message.

Lower confidence — transient spike in concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all slots simultaneously: if many agents were created close together and not yet cleaned up, slots would appear exhausted even if the quota is sufficient under normal load.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T17:45–17:52Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the VM provisioning step.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any new remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free capacity. The failure is localized to the Kubernetes peer-pod VM resource layer in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' scheduler message across all three sibling checks over a ~7-minute window.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. If the affinity were broadened or more nodes were labeled, capacity could be restored without changing VM slot limits.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM quota or cloud-provider limit reached at the infrastructure layer beneath Kubernetes: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is typically backed by a cloud VM quota; if that quota is exhausted, the device plugin would report 0 allocatable units on the eligible nodes, producing the same scheduler message.

Lower confidence — transient spike in concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all slots simultaneously: if many agents were created close together and not yet cleaned up, slots would appear exhausted even if the quota is sufficient under normal load.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 17:47 and 17:52 UTC on 2026-07-07 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence at all — every required field (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is missing from the check result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every attempt to create a remote agent pod times out unscheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval from reaching the agent creation step, causing a total absence of evidence and a contract validation failure for all five required fields. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 affinity-matching nodes is fully consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption is also unavailable, meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free slots.

Secondary: The pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of the 6 cluster nodes, and those 2 nodes happen to be at full kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or misconfigured, schedulable capacity is artificially limited.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or production workload may have created remote agent pods that were not cleaned up (e.g., withCleanup in the runner failed silently), consuming the available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and leaving none for subsequent runs.
Lower confidence: A cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm may have been reduced, shrinking the total available slots without a corresponding change to workload demand.

If no kata.peerpods.io/vm-consuming pods are found on the 2 matching nodes (i.e., the resource shows as fully available), the root cause would be a scheduler misconfiguration or resource quota policy rather than workload-driven exhaustion.

If the local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime checks (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) also fail at the same time, the failure scope would be broader than the remote agent pod scheduling layer.
